subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin-level config pre-apply veto hook, and what ordering and failure semantics should it have relative to built-in validation, SecretRef preflight, config.set/config.patch/config.apply, and shared mutation helpers?
rationale: This would become a public plugin/config mutation contract that executes near auth, provider routing, SecretRef, and persistence boundaries, so code inspection cannot safely choose fail-open/fail-closed behavior or the permanent SDK shape.

options.title: Approve guarded config-write hook
options.body: Define a narrow synchronous hook with typed context, redaction, timeout, recursion, and reject semantics before implementing it across all config mutation paths.

options.title: Defer to built-in validation only
options.body: Keep current schema, SecretRef, base-hash, and agent-tool allowlist protections and reject a plugin veto hook unless a stronger user need appears.

options.title: Fold into broader preflight RFC
options.body: Treat config-write interception as one part of a larger validation/preflight framework and keep this issue linked until that design chooses the boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded config-write hook
recommendation.body: Define a narrow synchronous hook with typed context, redaction, timeout, recursion, and reject semantics before implementing it across all config mutation paths.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the latest substantive routing comment on this issue and have recent adjacent config/security history.
